assign.outcome:
**All six landed. The bar keeps its row when you type an address, a page inside a page survives being saved, and the tab you marked as first now opens first on the page itself.**

![The seven words keep their row; the address gets the line under them, a field you can read, and a Copy](shots/bar-address-1280.png)

**1 — The address has its own full-width line.** `flex: 1 0 100%` on `.paging-address` is the whole of it: a 100% basis in a wrapping row always starts a new line. **Measured at 1280:** the five one-word groups are **57px tall on one baseline** (the CONTENT group was **106** against its siblings' 57, its label 50px higher, and *Draw it* wrapped). The field is **582px at 1280 and 2370px at 3440**, holding a 53-character address with nothing clipped — it was 153px showing 12 of 56. Beside it, **Draw it** and **Copy**, and the Copy reads the field **on the press** (`copy_chip` takes a getter now, or it would copy whatever the box held at page load).

**2 — A nested page survives being saved.** `nest` is a string in `mode` (a preset id, or a page's address) beside `blocks` and `default`, printed by **both** exports and read back by `stage_props()`. **Proved:** on `/imagine/paging/?nest=dashboard` I typed a name and pressed *Make this a page* — the file read `"nest": "dashboard"`, the printed `page.js` read `this.stage({…}, { nest: "dashboard" })`, and **the made page opened cold with the dashboard running inside its box**, wearing its own words, address bare. The bar on a page you made writes it too (`keep_nest`, the drawer's chip on `/make/notes/`). Both test files were deleted and `made/` is byte-identical by md5.

![The page I saved an hour ago, opened cold, with a whole other page running inside it](shots/nested-made-page-1280.png)

**3 — The default tab is read on the saved page.** One line in `stage_props()`. With `later` marked default, `/imagine/paging/make/notes/` opens on **Later**; `stage_props()` returns `open: 1`; and the printed `page.js` now has `open: 1` **under** the comment `// the tab that opens first`, which had no code beneath it.

**4 — The two url controls accept the same pages, and a miss tells the truth.** `page_at()` asks `nest_of()` first, so `?content=/imagine/paging/library/blog-post/` **runs that preset** — the same address `?nest=` has always taken. A miss now says *"Nothing here could be read at /framework/ui/"* and names the three addresses that work (a page you made, a ready-made page, a `.md` file) instead of claiming a page that exists does not. And an **off-site** `https://…` is a value the realm keeps, shows in the field, notes at the field and declares in the box — it used to be dropped while the url went on carrying it.

**5 — Build's bar owns the words.** The left column's Navigation, Content colour and Arrangement controls are gone; it is **Name · Blocks · Pages · Code**, and the card is two columns with two full-width rows under them. The file pane is **957 client on 957 scroll at 1280** (it was 287 on 455) and 2847/2847 at 3440, with its own scroll and a **Copy the file** button.

**6 — The small ones, all five.** Content's lede says the ninth answer in its first sentence; the twelve nest chips carry `aria-pressed`; `doc/mechanisms.md`, `doc/templates.md` and `build/readme.md` no longer teach `chips()`, `at("mech")`, `axes:` or `Template.Toolbar`; `kind_of()` is deleted; and every `page.json` is written **with a trailing newline**, so a save leaves no diff at all.

**Proof.** 65 urls × 400 / 1280 / 1920 / 3440 = **260 cold loads, one console line** — the known `readme/page.js` declared-child probe 404 — and **zero sideways scroll** at every width. Every number above was measured headless, not estimated.

**Left deliberately:** the trailing newline is added by a six-line `PageFile extends FileSaver` in `made.js` rather than in `ext/Saver`, which this task may not touch — the note beside it says so. `doc/decisions.md` still mentions `dress()`/`chips()`, and stays: it is a dated record of what was decided, not a page that teaches the code.
